//: Story Phase 3, chapter 14: The Grand Stenchmaster's Terms. An hour after the lure. Garrick comes back to the starboard davit (4,24); Jory does the damage report at the patch (14,21); Squawks is on his perch by the cabin (12,13). Ends with Garrick rowing off again and the second distant release (vista finale_release). Story Phase 3 stops there.

p3c6.begin.narrate: The sea around the Queen Anne's Revenge is flat and blue and empty. The crew keep looking at it anyway.

p3c6.lookout.text: ROWBOAT! ROWBOAT OFF THE STARBOARD QUARTER!

p3c6.lookout: hale[surprised]: It's him, Captain. He's coming back.
hale: Slowly. And... I think he's only got the one oar.

p3c6.lookout.tutorial: Garrick is coming alongside. Meet him at the starboard davit and haul him aboard.
p3c6.lookout.title: Grand Stenchmaster, Temporarily

p3c6.return: The rowboat comes alongside, very slowly.
There are bite marks all along the gunwale. One oar is missing. The other is shorter than it was.
And hanging from the stern by its teeth, swinging gently, is a small and very determined shark.
rook[surprised]: ...He's brought a friend.
rook: Heave!
The little shark lets go, drops back into the sea with a plop, and swims off looking thoroughly pleased with itself.
The Grand Stenchmaster climbs out onto the deck. He is soaked. His sideburns are standing straight out. His pot has a shark-shaped dent in it.
garrick[proud]: Captain.
garrick[proud]: I saved the ship.
brask[annoyed]: You got the ship HOLED.
jory[annoyed]: They chewed the rudder.
rook[annoyed]: We lost all the Frog Grog.
brask: They bit the port rail in three places. The captain got rejected by a shark.
garrick[businesslike]: All true. All regrettable. And yet...
garrick[proud]: ...some of the ship remains!
captain[resigned]: ...Some of the ship remains.
jory[surprised]: Captain. Port side. Look at the water.
Two sharks are drifting past the ship, belly up, turning in slow circles. Every so often one of them blows a small yellow bubble.
brask[surprised]: They're DRUNK. They're drunk on the Frog Grog.
garrick[delighted]: A hit with every demographic!
captain: Jory. Tell me what's left of my ship.
jory: Aye, Captain. Come and see the patch.

p3c6.return.tutorial: Hear Jory's damage report by the patched hull, midships to port.
p3c6.return.title: Grand Stenchmaster, Temporarily

p3c6.damage: jory: The patch is holding. Good oak, good nails. I'd not lean on it, but she won't take on water.
jory: The rudder's chewed all down the blade, but she turns. Nell's had to learn to steer a bit to the left.
jory[annoyed]: The port rail's bitten through in three places. The rowboat's bitten everywhere. We've one oar.
jory: And every drop of Frog Grog on the ship went over the side. The sharks had the lot.
jory: Gone, Captain. He took them for a walk, and they followed him.
jory[determined]: She'll sail. Battered, and she smells like a cheese that's died, but she'll sail.
captain[resigned]: That's all I ask of her.
jory: Garrick's been hovering, Captain. I think he wants a word. He's got that look.

p3c6.damage.tutorial: Garrick is waiting for a word. Hear him out.
p3c6.damage.title: Grand Stenchmaster, Temporarily

p3c6.terms: garrick[businesslike]: Captain. Now that the emergency's over, I thought we might discuss terms.
captain: Terms.
garrick: For my continued services. As Grand Stenchmaster.
captain[angry]: Fine. MY terms first.
captain: You report dangerous meals. Beans, cabbage, onion, garlic, cheese, sausage, eel. Anything like them. You tell me BEFORE it goes in.
garrick[proud]: Captain, with the greatest respect, the Grand Stenchmaster answers to no one.
captain[angry]: The Grand Stenchmaster absolutely answers to the captain.
garrick[nervous]: ...The Grand Stenchmaster absolutely answers to the captain.
garrick: He was only checking.
captain: Go on, then.
garrick[businesslike]: Jurisdiction. I'd like to be the man in charge whenever there's a stink emergency involving sharks.
captain: ...That's fair. That's actually fair.
garrick: And Frog Grog production.
captain: Mags keeps the key.
garrick[smug]: A shared-services arrangement. I can work with that.
garrick: And the water butt.
captain: What about the water butt?
garrick[pretend]: I had a look at it this morning, Captain. Nothing to worry about. There was a bubble.
You lift the lid of the drinking-water butt by the starboard rail and look in.
A single yellow bubble rises slowly from the bottom, reaches the surface, and pops.
garrick[proud]: Frog Water.
captain: No.
garrick: It's got a ring to it.
captain[angry]: Put the LID back on.
garrick[businesslike]: One last thing. Regular inspections of the captain's beard.
captain[angry]: Absolutely not.
Out on the starboard side, a single fin is cruising slowly past. It seems to be sniffing the air.
garrick: They'll be back, Captain. And when they come, they'll come for the strongest smell on the ship.
garrick[businesslike]: A regular sniff of the beard would give us plenty of warning. Shark forecasting.
captain[resigned]: ...From a safe distance.
garrick[delighted]: From a very safe distance!
garrick[queasy]: Hhhk.
garrick[businesslike]: ...Beard still terrible. I'll put it in the log.
garrick: Oh, and Captain? Squawks has been asking for you. Something about his head.

p3c6.terms.tutorial: Check on Squawks, on his perch by the cabin.
p3c6.terms.title: Grand Stenchmaster, Temporarily

p3c6.squawks: squawks[worried]: Captain. Captain! Come here. Look. Look at my head.
He shuffles out of his blanket and ducks his bald little head at you.
Right on top, where there was nothing at all this morning, there's a single, tiny, brand new feather.
It's yellow.
Not the green of the rest of him. Not the red of his old crest. Yellow. The exact yellow of everything else on this ship.
wick[concerned]: Captain, is that—
squawks[worried]: What colour, Captain? Can't see it. It's on my HEAD.

then: captain[tender]: It's a very special colour. It's golden. A golden feather.

p3c6.squawks: squawks[surprised]: Golden?
captain[tender]: Golden.
squawks[smug]: ...GOLDEN! Golden feather! Squawks is a GOLDEN parrot!
wick[happy]: ...It's very golden, Squawks.
garrick[delighted]: A new feather! Congratulations, Captain Squawks. May I?
garrick[proud]: Ah, yes. That's one of mine.
squawks[furious]: ...
squawks[outraged]: YOURS?!
You look out along your ship.
At the patch on the port side, holding. At the sails, breathing in and out. At the crew, with socks on their faces, cheering on a bald parrot as it chases a man in a curtain round the mainmast.
At the fins, back again, circling at a respectful distance.
At Garrick. Who, somehow, in a single afternoon, has turned out to be useful.
captain: ...GARRICK.
Squawks takes the opportunity to bite him on the ankle.
captain[resigned]: The title. Grand Stenchmaster.
garrick[nervous]: ...Yes, Captain?
captain[resigned]: You can keep it.
garrick[surprised]: I can?
captain[determined]: TEMPORARILY.
garrick[delighted]: It's OFFICIAL!
garrick[proud]: The best appointments always start temporarily, Captain! It's how you know they're going to last!
captain[resigned]: That's not how it works.
squawks[insulting]: Grand. Stench. Tempor-arily.
Everyone on deck freezes.
garrick[nervous]: ...That wasn't the ship.
squawks[furious]: DEADLY BREW! DEADLY BREEEEW! EVERYBODY UPWIND!
hale[alarmed]: Captain, is that an emergency? Is that an official emergency now?
captain[determined]: It is now. Any noise out of that stomach that isn't a word is an emergency. All hands.

p3c6.squawks.tutorial: Suspicious stomach noises are now an official emergency. Get Garrick into the rowboat at the starboard davit. Again.
p3c6.squawks.title: Grand Stenchmaster, Temporarily

p3c6.evacuate: garrick[nervous]: Captain, I have JUST come back.
garrick: I have BITE marks. I have bite marks on my BITE marks. There's ONE oar!
jory: Frying pan, Captain. From the galley. Paddles near enough the same.
jim[sad]: And the rest of the beans. There were more. There are always more.
captain: Row until the water changes colour. Then keep going.

p3c6.evacuate.text: ANOTHER OCEAN! I KNOW! I KNOW!

p3c6.evacuate: One by one, the fins peel away from the ship and follow the little rowboat toward the horizon.

p3c6.finale.narrate: And so, late in the afternoon, the Queen Anne's Revenge sailed on.
Her sails breathed in and out with no wind at all. Her deck was stained the colour of old mustard.
Her crew drank the last of the Frog Grog from the galley, because it was all there was, and made faces, and drank it anyway.
Her hull held, patched with good oak. Her ropes sweated gently in the sun.
Her bell rang the hour, and coughed.
At her wheel stood Captain Stinkbeard, terror of the Sapphire Sea, with a small, bald, blanketed parrot at his elbow, sporting one golden feather.
And somewhere behind her, at a respectful distance, the sharks came trailing after.

p3c6.finale.text: ...DIES AND GENTLEMEN OF THE QUEEN ANNE'S REVENGE...!

p3c6.finale: Every hand on deck grabs the nearest solid thing. Squawks disappears entirely under his blanket.

p3c6.finale.narrate: Far across the water, a vast yellow cloud rose into the afternoon sky. The sea rippled out from under it in great slow rings.
Every shark for a mile turned, and went to have a look.
And carried back on the breeze, very faintly, came the sound of one extremely satisfied man, laughing.

p3c6.coda: Captain Stinkbeard's ship still smells. It will smell, according to the Grand Stenchmaster, for centuries.
The Grand Stenchmaster himself is somewhere over the horizon, in another ocean. For now.

p3c6.coda.tutorial: Story Phase 3 is complete. The ship is yours to explore: the crew have plenty to say about the Grand Stenchmaster, and the Stench Log is in your pause menu. The story continues in the next chapter.
p3c6.coda.title: To Be Continued
